To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the treatment of ligamentous injuries of the thumb metacarpophalan-geal joint depends on the severity of the injury, and that surgical treatment is recommended for injuries of type 2 and 3, and for injuries of type I in cases of a severe instability.

1) the treatment of thumb base joint instability should be conservative in all patients without any dislocation, 2) in all patients with a dislocation the treatment should be surgical, 3) the surgical treatment should be performed by open reduction and ligamentous repair, 4) if a dislocated fragment is too large to be reduced and fixed, a K-wire should be used for fixation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points: a) the diagnosis, b) the conservative treatment, c) the surgical treatment and d) the results of the surgical treatment.

the following aspects of the ligamentous injuries of the base joint of the thumb: a. the frequency of ligamentous injuries in alpine skiers and ski-skaters, b. the frequency of osseous ruptures with dislocation of fragments and without any dislocation, c. the results of surgical and conservative therapy in 106 patients, d. the frequency of instability after conservative therapy in 64 patients and e. the results of surgery in 44 patients.
the diagnosis and the treatment of ligamentous ruptures of the metacapophalangeal thumb joint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conservative therapy is not sufficient in most patients.
the treatment of choice for a ligamentous rupture of the ulnar side of the metacapophalangeal thumb joint is the surgical reconstruction of the ligament.
the treatment of choice is the open reduction with internal fixation and the ligamentous repair of the base of the thumb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conservative treatment should be limited to ligamentous ruptures with a stable joint.
the treatment of ligament injuries of the thumb base is not always conservative, because in many cases the ligament will not be healed by conservative treatment and will be unstable.
conservative treatment is not indicated if the patient wants to return to sports and that the results after surgical treatment are better than those reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ligamentous instability after conservative treatment is high, and the instability after surgical treatment is low.
the use of the UCL graft in conjunction with a suture anchor for repair of the UCL is a safe and effective method for the management of chronic, symptomatic UCL injuries.
the use of an arthroscopic technique is a safe and effective method for treating thumb MCP joint instability.
